body.x: Identifying a material by its spectral signature has traditionally meant a lab-based spectrometer, not a component built into the product that needs the information.
Could that capability fit inside a sensor small enough for a washing machine or a food processing line?

MantiSpectra B.V., an ISO 9001-certified company founded in 2020 as a spin-off from Eindhoven University of Technology and led by CEO Giuseppe Coppola, designs and manufactures ChipSense, a broadband hyperspectral sensor component. At KES 2026, the company is exhibiting ChipSense to deepen its engagement with Korean makers of professional and consumer electronics.

ChipSense is a near-infrared and short-wave infrared (NIR/SWIR) sensor that uses a computational spectroscopy approach. According to the company, it delivers prediction accuracy comparable to lab-based spectrometers across multiple uses, and it identifies and characterizes materials in real time without damaging them. It covers a spectral range of 500 to 1,700 nm and captures 64 broad, overlapping spectral bands in a single shot. The company says the sensor needs no per-device calibration and can be reused across applications. It is made through monolithic wafer-level integration of indium gallium arsenide (InGaAs) photodetectors and optical filters, an approach the company says supports high manufacturing yield and consistent device performance at competitive cost.

MantiSpectra launched ChipSense in September 2025, after defining its specifications in 2024. Five customers have deployed it in operational applications, all in the professional market with sensor-based subsystems, and the company says several more companies in professional and consumer markets are evaluating it, including large home appliance makers. It has shipped products to countries mostly in Europe, Southeast Asia and North America.

The initial focus is industrial edge AI, IoT and robotics, targeting OEMs and ODMs of sensor-enabled devices and suppliers of sensor subsystems for automation and humanoid robotics. Key markets include food and beverage, agritech, semiconductors, pharmaceuticals and recycling, followed by health monitoring in wearables, point-of-care devices and endoscopy, and smart consumer appliances that could use material recognition to choose a laundry cycle or guide food preparation. MantiSpectra sells directly and through component manufacturers, OEMs and ODMs, engineering R&D partners and photonics distributors, and says it needs customers with a strong innovation mindset to shape new product categories.

KES 2026, the 57th Korea Electronics Show, runs Oct. 13 to Oct. 16 at COEX Halls A and B in Seoul. Alongside the co-located XR & Spatial Computing Show, the event features X-SPACE 2026, a special exhibition covering digital twins, industrial XR, spatial intelligence, XR devices and spatial computing platforms. The Innovation Awards ceremony takes place on Oct. 13.
